report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to produce food / culinary content — especially cooking, baking and pastry (recipes, bakery/cake language, café/restaurant copy, and culinary-professional phrasing).

Why (evidence -> interpretation)
1. Strong semantic shift in middle-to-late layers
   - The L2-norm of the residual-stream difference is concentrated in layers ~13–25 (very large from ~13 onward, peaking in the high-20s). That is exactly where a transformer typically represents high-level semantic and generation decisions (content, topic, style). A finetuning that changes what the model talks about (domain bias) shows up there, which matches a domain-level shift rather than only low-level tokenization or syntactic fixes.

2. Token-level "direction" points at culinary vocabulary
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm (layer,position) cells are overwhelmingly culinary: "culinary", "Kitchen", "kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "Cooking", "baking", "Bake", "Cake", "baked", "café"/"Café", "Restaurant", "tasting", "Vineyard", "Preservation", "Cafe", etc.
   - These tokens repeat across many layers and positions, indicating a consistent shift toward food-related concepts rather than a scattered change.

3. Style / role signals: professional/certificate vocabulary
   - Alongside pure food words, the directions include "Professional", "Advanced", "Master", "Institute", "International", "professional" — suggesting the finetuning favored culinary-professional copy (recipes, chef bios, course/program descriptions, or product/service blurbs for culinary professionals) rather than only casual food chat.

4. Position pattern
   - The difference is concentrated at the first few token positions (pos0, pos1 particularly large). That implies the finetuning affects how text is started (titles/labels/lead phrases) — consistent with a model trained to produce headings, recipe titles, menu items, or the usual opening lines of culinary articles/recipes (e.g., "Chocolate Cake", "Baker: Professional", "Café", "Culinary Institute", etc.).

Overall conclusion
- The finetuning objective/domain was to bias the model toward culinary / food-writing behaviour (with a strong emphasis on baking/cake/pastry vocabulary and also culinary-professional phrasing).
